From the patent files

Invention,
on paper.

Patent applications have always depended on explaining how an invention works. These patents from Nikola Tesla and Alexander Graham Bell illustrate the importance of detailed technical descriptions and drawings. That same attention to technical detail remains important today.

Explore patent counsel ↗
Experience behind the perspective

I speak law.
And code.

Before I became a lawyer, I was a software engineer. I’ve built apps, helped turn copyright law into software, and co-invented patented video surveillance technology.

That experience shapes how I work with clients on software contracts, open-source issues, licensing, and patents: understand how the technology works, then connect the legal advice to the product and the business. Learn more about my work as a software patent attorney.

More about my background ↗

Find me on GitHub ↗

01

Patents from the inventor’s side.

I’m a co-inventor of video surveillance technology involving image processing and object tracking. My issued U.S. patents, each titled Video surveillance system, include 7,859,564, 7,956,889, and 8,605,155. I bring that experience of developing an invention to my work as a patent attorney.

02

The Durationator: copyright law in code.

At Tulane, I helped develop the logic representation language and engine for the Durationator, software for analyzing copyright terms worldwide. Professor Elizabeth Townsend Gard’s article about that work was cited by Justice Breyer in his Supreme Court dissent in Golan v. Holder, 565 U.S. 302, 357 (2012).

03

The first Louisiana Civil Code app for iPhone.

In 2009, I developed and released the first Louisiana Civil Code iOS app, putting a searchable legal reference in lawyers’ pockets. It was a practical way to bring my work in software and law together.

Common questions.

A few useful
starting points.

What kinds of legal matters do you handle?

I handle patent applications and disputes, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, software licensing, software development agreements, and other technology-related intellectual property matters.

What is your technical background?

I studied computer science at Duke University and worked as a software engineer before becoming an attorney. I've developed web applications, worked with databases and Linux systems, and written software for commercial and legal applications. I'm also a named inventor on three issued U.S. patents.

Can you help with software contracts and open-source issues?

Yes. I work on software development and licensing agreements, including ownership of code, third-party software, licensing terms, and open-source compliance. My software engineering background helps me understand how these issues arise in actual development projects.

Where do you practice?

I'm based in Kean Miller's New Orleans office. I'm licensed in Louisiana and registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Representation in other jurisdictions depends on the matter and applicable rules.

How can I contact you?

You can reach me at Kean Miller at 504.620.3356 or matthew.miller@keanmiller.com. Please don't send confidential information before an attorney-client relationship has been established.

Your next step

working on?

If you need assistance with a patent, trademark, copyright, software agreement, or other intellectual property matter, contact me at Kean Miller to discuss whether I can help.
